canonical_name: Congruence invariance of inertia for finite real symmetric matrices
literal_source_claim_zh: 实对称矩阵正负惯性指数在合同下不变
literal_source_claim_en: The positive and negative inertia indices of a real symmetric matrix are invariant under congruence.
statement_blocker: The catalog does not fix the finite matrix index, define congruence or its equation orientation, choose an invertible-matrix representation, define positive and negative inertia indices by eigenvalue multiplicity, diagonal signs, or maximal definite-subspace dimension, state whether the zero index is included, or settle zero-dimensional and degenerate cases. A modern source and close mathlib quadratic-form declarations are leads, but their specialization and matrix transport are not accepted source-to-target mappings. Selecting an exact Lean proposition at intake would invent clauses or substitute the abstract quadratic-form theorem for the literal matrix claim.
domain_and_universes: Open: an approved source must fix real square matrices indexed by Fin n or another finite type, or finite-dimensional real quadratic spaces, and the universe and decidability conventions.
conclusion: Open: equality of the positive and negative inertia indices for congruent real symmetric matrices; the definitions and whether zero inertia is explicit remain unresolved.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded before a proposition is selected; the statement phase must resolve every case in scope-map.md.
candidate_scope_not_credited: for real symmetric A and B, an invertible P with B = transpose P * A * P implies equality of their positive and negative eigenvalue counts
equivalent finite-dimensional real quadratic forms have equal QuadraticForm.sigPos and QuadraticForm.sigNeg
every finite-dimensional real quadratic form is equivalent to a weighted sum of squares with weights in {-1, 0, 1}
the inertia triple of positive, negative, and zero indices is invariant under congruence
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: empty and singleton finite index types
zero, positive definite, negative definite, and indefinite matrices
whether the zero inertia index is explicit or derived from fixed dimension
excluded_substitutions: existence of a diagonalization without uniqueness of sign counts

similarity invariance rather than congruence invariance
positive-definiteness preservation, rank invariance, or determinant-sign invariance alone
nondegenerate, positive definite, diagonal, fixed-dimension, or numerical special cases

the catalog's untrusted verified label or discovery probe as proof credit
